_comment: THE PROJECT'S SCOPE, AS DATA. Read by the site (src/content/nations.js and
src/content/storms.js) and by the cleaning scripts (data-pipeline/common.py).
It is JSON rather than JS because Python cannot import a module, and a roster
that disagrees with itself across two languages is exactly what the
exclusions section exists to rule out.
What belongs here: facts the stated rule determines -- which storms are in,
which nations each struck, and the year window the data covers. What does NOT
belong here: prose. Per-storm profiles, leads, notes and citations live in
src/content/storms.js, which merges them onto these entries by id and throws
at import time if either side is missing an entry the other has.
THE RULE: a severe tropical cyclone that made landfall or had major impact in
two or more of the four in-scope nations, between rosterStart and rosterEnd.
yearMin opens in 2013, not at rosterStart: a chart of an event year is
meaningless without baseline years before it, and two clear years ahead of
the earliest storm is the minimum that lets a reader see what normal was.
